slides.title: SAM has 10 WHO steps.
slides.sub: Diagnosis, the 10 steps in order, and the **3 things you must not give**.

slides.title: Is it SAM?
rows: Oedema, **failed appetite test** or a medical complication
Good appetite, no complication: **RUTF** in community

slides.title: Steps 1–3
slides.tagline: the killers of the first days.
rows: Glucose **< 54 mg/dL**: **50 mL 10% glucose** oral/NG. Unconscious: **10% dextrose 5 mL/kg IV**
Axillary **< 35 °C**: skin-to-skin, cover head, warm room
**ReSoMal 5 mL/kg every 30 min** × 2 h, then **5–10 mL/kg/h** up to 10 h
Start at once, **2-hourly, day and night**

slides.title: Steps 4–7
rows: Antibiotics for **all**: amoxicillin if well, **ampicillin + gentamicin** if complicated
Vitamin A, folic acid, zinc, copper from day 1

slides.title: Steps 8–10
slides.tagline: appetite is back. now catch up.
rows: To **F-100** when appetite returns & oedema reduces
F-100 / RUTF **150–220 kcal/kg/day**, protein **4–6 g/kg/day**. **Start iron**

slides.text: Weight gain per kg per day in rehabilitation is ==good==. **5–10** is moderate. **< 5** is poor: look for infection or a feeding problem.
slides.note: Discharge: MUAC ≥ 12.5 cm or WHZ ≥ −2 SD, and no oedema for at least 2 weeks.
checks: **No IV fluids** unless in shock (15 mL/kg over 1 h)
**No iron** until the child is gaining weight

caption:
SAM has 10 WHO steps. The first week decides survival 🥣

📏 SAM (6–59 mo), any one: MUAC < 11.5 cm · WHZ < −3 SD · bilateral pitting oedema. Admit if oedema, failed appetite test or a medical complication.

🔴 Week 1 (stabilisation)
1 Hypoglycaemia < 54 mg/dL → 50 mL 10% glucose (unconscious: 10% dextrose 5 mL/kg IV)
2 Hypothermia < 35 °C → skin-to-skin, warm
3 Dehydration → ReSoMal 5 mL/kg every 30 min × 2 h, then 5–10 mL/kg/h
4 K 3–4 & Mg 0.4–0.6 mmol/kg/day
5 Antibiotics for all
6 Vitamin A, folate, zinc, copper
7 F-75, 130 mL/kg/day, 2 → 3 → 4-hourly

🟢 Weeks 2–6 (rehabilitation)
8 F-100/RUTF 150–220 kcal/kg/day, protein 4–6 g/kg/day, start iron
9 Play & care
10 Follow-up plan

📈 Target gain > 10 g/kg/day
✅ Discharge: MUAC ≥ 12.5 cm or WHZ ≥ −2 SD, no oedema for 2 weeks
🚫 Week 1: no IV unless shock · no diuretics · no iron

💾 Save for your NRC posting
📩 Send to your NEET-PG group
